review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Can you give a brief summary about this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Sora is a filler character that can resupply the team's HP and boost their attack power, albeit not impressively nor constantly unless given certain conditions. Sora's weakness lies in her unmusical kit, seemingly an output by a random kit generator which screams mediocrity. She has skills that increase her own HP potency, which is useless in 99% of game modes (except PvP but very arguable); a team Storage skill that depends on part destruction (which is clunky at its finest and a hyper niche), but at least it comes with a modest ATK buff when those parts are broken; but is overshadowed by a 40s Burst Skill that heals and dispels debuff (this one is the least impressive probably).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Analyzing her kit, we theorize that Sora's usage will be similar to Maxwell's and Crust's, in that she will be used in the off-burst to provide the team with an offensive buff and an occasional supporting effect. This, however, results in team-building inflexibility as you are forced to run a 2-1-2 — no compromise there. This makes her weak, alongside the trifling S1 effect. However, the dispel can still come useful against bosses or certain enemies in PvP (such as Blanc), but strictly for PvE, we believe Crust, who is a more reliable cleanser, has greater versatility. Note that Crust cannot be used in PvP.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"In terms of usage, we don't really see Sora being used anywhere, since she is not meta or does not excel in any niche. The only sensible argument is that she is technically the only cleanser with true healing (Ade doesn't heal, btw). However, we haven't really encountered a situation where we can't just work around it (e.g. like using Helm). Unfortunately, this means, if you like her, you will only be pulling for collection or eye candy.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"PvP is another question, but it's not good news, either. Sora isn't really better than the current B1 options we have. Firstly, she's not a clip RL. Secondly, she is a Supporter, which means her defense stat is not that high, and her being Wind doesn't help. All these, in addition to her lack of innate Damage Reduction/Max HP, makes her too squishy for P1 tanking. Her HP potency will only be useful if she receives healing, and sure, her Burst does heal, but what makes her better than, let's say, Noise and Rapunzel, who have superb additional effects? Not to mention, there are no parts in PvP, so RIP S2!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"In conclusion, Sora is just a filler unit, made to satisfy the lust of people who like her design. She's not made to penetrate the meta in any way.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Should I get this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"No","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Skip her at all costs, unless she is waifu enough for you. Normally, we still recommend pulling situational units for tryhard UR and SR players, but this time we fully encourage skipping. We just don't see any potential in her, so save your gems and resist any temptation to spend. NieR is returning too. While they don't have the most broken units, getting them just for the sake of collection is still better than getting Sora.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Do you want dupes?","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Well, she does grant the team ATK buff based on her base ATK stat, but no, please no. In fact, we shall cleanse you for having thought of such an unholy idea in the first place.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Gold mileage worthy?","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Again, no, and we should not be reminding you of this anymore. We've said no four times in this section, and now we've said it five times. She's not worth mileage at all, not even as a wishlist character!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Usage Analysis and Tier List","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Campaign (LD) - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"D","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" | Campaign (HD) - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"D","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Mobs usually don't have parts. Some do in late Campaign, but they are rare and not as big of a threat. When there are mobs with parts, Sora can buff the team's ATK, so she is not that bad, but when there aren't, she is just Emma V2. We placed Emma in D tier, so there Sora goes.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Bossing - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"C","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"She is not the worst option for Bossing, but she surely isn’t one of the better options. She is quite literally mid, as she still provides some ATK buffs if the boss has regular destructible parts, e.g. Kraken. She can also heal the team when needed (please treat her Burst as emergency healing instead of alternate Burst; do not mind if the Storage is empty).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"One probably strong point of Sora is that she can prepare for a powerful boss attack far beforehand. You see, as long as parts continue being destroyed, her Storage won't disappear. So, if you trigger Storage then fill it up with Burst (or other sources of healing), you can make use of the HP padding even 1 minute into the future. We don't see this technique being useful anywhere, though. Maybe against Black Snake?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Sora can also cleanse. Against bosses that apply debilitating debuffs once at the start of the battle, Sora can be a strong pick. Why not bosses that apply debuffs frequently? Well, because ideally you want to avoid using Sora's Burst Skill, which doesn't give ATK power (unless you need the healing every 26-30 seconds somehow). It's almost always better to use your other B1's Burst Skill, which hopefully is a strong DMG buffer like Liter/Siren/Rapipi or even Miranda (with a B2 CDR).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"That said, Sora as a sole cleanser is overshadowed by the likes of Crust, which can cleanse more often and whose cleanses are always available on demand. Crust also provides a very strong offensive effect as both in-burst and off-burst B2 without relying on parts. Sora's only lead over her is that she has emergency healing, but surely there are other ways to tackle this problem.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"All these make Sora more of a niche character with no real use. She can be used in UR, but there are better options. If you are pulling her, you are not pulling her for meta, but for her meaty thighs.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"PVP - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"C","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"C-tier because she is similar to Pascal in many ways, perhaps worst in most cases because she has lower burst generation than Pascal. She simply doesn't reach the bar for B tier — Sora's weakness is her \"empty\" kit and the innate unreliability of instant non-padding HP recovery skills. Note that her Storage ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"does not","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" activate in PvP, so her healing is non-padding there.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"First of all, Sora has a generic healer kit. She has HP potency, which means she heals more from healing(s), and also recovers the team's HP by using Burst Skill. However, as we explained in the Skill Analysis - Burst Skill section, instant HP recovery are worse than Max HP skills in PvP. This is because it doesn't really block one-shot wipes or continuous, devastating attacks like SAnis's (since healing cannot exceed Max HP without Storage).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"What about the HP potency? Well, Sora is not tanky enough to be placed in P1. Unlike Noise, she doesn't have Damage Reduction or Max HP▲, so she relies solely on stat and healing from teammates (thanks to HP potency). This is not enough in PvP, especially if you fight against Fire enemies (Sora is Wind). If you have to survive in P1 from your teammates' healing, why don't you just use Nero or maybe Moran or maybe just Noise or Rapunzel with stun threats? Sora doesn't really offer much here. Her presence isn't threatening enough.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"That said, Sora is not completely useless. For newer players who do not have enough burst generation units, Sora's mediocre burst generation is on an acceptable level of usability. With the severe lack of b1 units initially in PvP, Sora is at the very least usable for incomplete rosters to fill in empty slots.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"document"}

skillAnalysis.raw: {"nodeType":"document","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"heading-2","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Kit Analysis","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Sora is a regular RL user, not a clip RL, so her Burst Gen is not that high. She also has a reload time of 2.0s, which is very long. This makes her a bit clunky to use, and her gameplay feel should be similar to Maiden: Ice Rose.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-5","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Skill 1 - Just One Effect. In 2025. That's Barely Beneficial.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Sora gains increased HP potency immediately upon entering battle, receiving increased recovery from all sources of healing. However, the value is just ~35%, very light and inconsequential. Not only that, usually the amount of healing we get from healers in PvE right now is already enough, and an extra 35% for herself won't help. It's either you need healing or you don't; nothing in between. If anything, it should have been HP potency for the whole team, not just herself. What's the use of her surviving but the team dying anyway?","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Moreover, in PvP, as this is a one-time effect that triggers at the start of battle and cannot be triggered again, it can easily be dispelled and countered by Rosanna (assuming she is one of the two units that have the highest ATK). This makes the skill even less impactful. The only way it can be of use is when you try to tank with her and somehow inject a lot of healing (such as w/ Rapunzel). Still, why just don't use alternative units and compositions?","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-5","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Skill 2 - A One Liner Again in 2025","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Sora grants the team the buff Storage and increased ATK power for 15 seconds whenever a part is destroyed. The Storage buff can stack up to 5 times.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"blockquote","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"### What is Storage?","marks":[{"type":"bold"},{"type":"underline"}],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Storage is a buff that grants a unit increased Max HP in the form of HP padding. This means it doesn't \"literally\" affect their Max HP number, but it's there as an \"extra HP bar\". This extra HP bar stores excess HP, so when damage is taken, this bar will eat the damage first until it depletes before actual HP is consumed. You can treat it as a shield if you want, but shields can block attacks that are stronger than them (won't eat actual HP). Note that Storage doesn't affect Max HP-dependent skills like healing, conversion (2B/Cinderella), and \"gain X if Max HP at 100%\".","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Having explained that, let's discuss this skill's three major problems:","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"unordered-list","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Not all enemies have parts, and even if they do, they may not have adequate uptime. Good luck finding a boss that suits her — not like you planned to use her for mobbing, right? Right?","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The offensive buff scales off caster's ATK, but building her is not worthwhile at all. You should not be wasting your gear sets, rocks, credits, and even skill mats improving her from very weak to weak, especially in the current economy.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Storage doesn't heal, and it only stores excess recovery, which means there must be subsequent healing to utilize it. This is different from Marciana, who actually heals thanks to her S2 effect, making it as if her Storage were the one healing. Sora does have a healing ability — her Burst — but is using it worthwhile? You will probably end up using it only during emergencies.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"We will leave the application of this skill analysis to you, but to summarize, we just treat it as an off-burst buffing skill. It can be activated without having to use Burst Skill, so as long as enemy parts are there and are destroyed regularly, Sora can continually empower the team and boost their survivability. It's just that her values are too low for her to compete with alternatives like Crust (who is not reliant on parts), Maxwell (who is also not reliant on parts), Privaty, Mast: Romantic Maid, etc, assuming all of them are equally built.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The Storage part is rather useless. We don't see the point of it. If you want to use Sora, in most fights, you will want to avoid using her Burst Skill because it doesn't buff the team offensively. This renders her Storage useless, unless someone else is healing/filling it. Sure, there might be edge cases for when you want to use her Burst Skill, but for every problem she solves, there are other, more efficient and economic, solutions to it.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-5","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Burst Skill - One-Liners Again. Congrats, She Only Has Three Lines of Skills.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Upon using Burst Skill, Sora immediately heals the team a large amount and dispels 1 debuff.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"blockquote","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The dispel prioritizes the most first debuff applied, which makes it predictable and viable for targeting certain hostile debuffs in PvP (by controlling FB speed). However, this also makes it less flexible as she cannot dispel newer debuffs randomly by chance. ","marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"data":{}},{"nodeType":"text","value":"Note that some debuffs cannot be dispelled.","marks":[{"type":"bold"},{"type":"italic"}],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"What makes this skill good, though, is most likely the healing, which is a lot. In PvE, this has limited usage because a separate B1 healer (that works by giving an emergency healing on Burst) is usually not needed nowadays, and even if you do need healing, there are options such as Anchor: Innocent Maid and Helm (Treasure). In PvP, Sora can be a decent option, but she's not better than her rivals, such as Noise and Rapunzel, who provide remarkable extra effects.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The problem with Sora's healing is that it isn't Max HP, so it doesn't really block instant wipes, like Noise can. It's also not like Rapunzel's who can revive and effectively counter certain Rosanna teams. That makes Sora closest in power and playstyle to Pascal (NieR freebie unit).","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"On another note, Sora's Burst Skill has a CD of 40s, making it unideal for PvE usage due to imposing a 2-1-2 formation. While that is not inherently a problem, Sora's lack of impact exacerbates it. Nevertheless, this shouldn't be a problem in PvP, since fights normally don't last a long time and survivability is as important as offensive power.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"However, pay attention to unit positioning. Note that Sora is almost, if not entirely, useless if she is not Bursting, unlike other healers. This is because her HP potency is barely advantageous and S2 is inactive. review.raw: {"nodeType":"document","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The partner in crime of Naga, Tia comes swooping down with magnificence as she explodes her enemies into ashes with her lizardry (buttons, I mean). She boasts a unique kit as a B1 Defender, which is already uncommon per se, that can help the team withstand more attacks and output more damage. With a noteworthy boost to Attack DMG, an occasional screen-wide taunt, frequent cover repairs, and the ability to erect Independent Shields for everyone in the team, Tia can ensure that her team remain a serious threat even with fewer DPS. To be more specific, she comes with an inherent drawback—you are forced to run a 2-1-2 formation.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-2","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Usage","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia and Naga are a solid duo, and they will be seeing a lot of use in Raids and Campaign. However, Tia straight up has some a major downside of using her—her taunt, which might pose a survival risk. She may require meticulous micromanagement and manual gameplay from time to time, which may discourage pairing her with other manual-heavy Nikkes like Alice. However, this does not mean they can't be paired. We will keep this point in mind as we delve deeper into her use. This restriction can prove to be rather serious at times.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia and Naga together can provide more buffs than any other pair that is present currently in-game. Even in non-ideal conditions for this Tiga (Tia and Naga) pair, at similar investments with Blanc and Noir, they will approximately provide equal buffs to the team when comparing both teams. At ideal conditions, they edge over the Bunny Pair (Blanc and Noir) by ~25% more!","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-6","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"CAMPAIGN","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia and Naga unlock a variety of team compositions and styles, in which you can focus more on dealing damage and denying enemy attacks with the help of Tia's taunt and shield. They are more difficult to play but can be rewarding. Some playtesting shows that they can allow you to clear stages you normally can't with Centi or Blanc Noir.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"A couple of perks they have over them are:","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"unordered-list","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Firstly, due to Tia being RL, she can provide better burst generation for the team that is less dependent on enemy distance.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Secondly, the Tiga pair provides buffs to the team, while the main source of damage in Bunny Pair is debuffs on enemies. The reason why buffs are better than debuffs in campaign is that these debuffs are applied only to the current wave of raptures. If the current wave dies and the next one starts, or some raptures have delayed spawns in the current wave, these new enemies will not have the debuffs applied to them, and hence damage output can be severely impacted.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Which also obviously comes with some disadvantages:","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"unordered-list","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia's constant taunt, which can cause her to be quite annoying to use. This can either seriously increase the skill requirement needed to beat a stage, or make it impossible for Tia to survive against waves of raptures. Hence, the Bunny Pair or Centi may just be the easier alternative for casual players. Against Laser Raptures, Tia can lose her shield if she gets shot even once, rendering her skill 1's Attack Damage Buff useless.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"list-item","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Another disadvantage is that the Bunny Pair has significantly higher healing, due to Blanc's teamwide and almost constant heals, in contrast to to Naga's focused healing every 5 shots. This is an extremely prevalent problem that Tia-Naga pair faces against Gas Raptures that constantly deal AoE damage, even through cover.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"To circumvent these drawbacks, normally you should try to kill raptures faster than they can kill you. This holds extremely true when pushing hard mode in campaign where the CP deficit can absolutely crush players as their Nikkes can get one-shot. However, Tia and Naga counterbalance this by offering relevant offensive buffs with high uptime that can be used to your advantage with certain key units like Alice, Modernia, Scarlet or A2 to quickly finish off the waves of enemy raptures. Furthermore, delaying Tia's taunt with careful manual use can do wonders in a stage for your survivability, as it can spread damage taken across your team.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"blockquote","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Here's a trick (not a secret): towards the end of some stages, a lot of times you might be able to just let Tia die and taunt the damage away from your main DPS, who can focus on the Stage Target in order to clear the stage, which is all that matters.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"heading-6","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"UNION RAID","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Being the second inseparable pair after Blanc & Noir who can provide more offensive buffs than them while being more restrictive, Tia & Naga are expected to see tons of usage in Union Raids, if not permanent. Tia & Naga will be used more against bosses with cores. Against Solo Bosses such as those in Union Raid, Tia and Naga will shine bright. Outperforming the Bunny Pair in offensive support, they will also provide some extra survivability to teams, and will absolutely crush non-wall bosses (usually the 1st, 2nd and 4th boss in a Union Raid). They will also prove to be an excellent choice against Nihilister, which has been a struggle for players due to the lack of cover heal skills (previous choices used to be Liter, Biscuit, and Cocoa).","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"blockquote","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Remember that Tia and Naga pair needs another B1 CDR unit to be paired with her due to re-entering Burst 1 stage. Hence, the team comp is restricted to a 2-1-2 setup, which means Modernia, the best option to get core hit buffs on, is essentially nerfed for this team in bossing since her ideal is a 1-1-3 setup where she does not burst.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"heading-6","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"SOLO RAID","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia & Naga's main battlefield is Solo Raid. Like in Union Raid, Tia & Naga will easily be in one of your top teams alongside your best DPS to help them survive and dish out immense damage within 3 minutes. They are still usable against bosses with no core, despite not being able to reach maximum performance. Quite flexible and allows effortless runs without retrying. In the on-going Modernia Solo Raid, Tia has proven herself to be quite the utility to have. Her shield is the ultimate counter to Modernia's lasers, her Attack Damage buff is almost always there, and she's always ready to help Naga activate her skills. The Tiga Pair has seen massive use, and all these teams were seen doing high damage. They aren't going anywhere soon, hopefully.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"blockquote","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Uniquely, there have also been cases in top scores where Tia was separated from Naga, while Naga was used as a buffer/healer for another team. This might be partly due to the fact that Naga and Guillotine have clashing kits (heals), but at the same time Tia's taunt is similar to Noise's, which is something Guillotine desires.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]},{"nodeType":"heading-6","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"PVP","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia is, well, just average in PvP. She offers nothing special to break the meta, but you can use her in some specific teams. Her taunt at 5 RL can be disheartening, taking a long time to set in, while the added delay from Re-Enter Burst I will slow your team down. Shield is also kind of useless as it does not block wipes. Nevertheless, she can create some interesting formations with double B1, if you place her in P1 alongside Biscuit. As a B1 defender, she can utilize Biscuit's S2 and also allow you to use other B2 skills. The extra damage from Skill 1 might be something worth looking into as well.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-6","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"MISSILIS TOWER","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia & Naga pair may be the best units in Missilis Tower, similar to what Blanc & Noir may provide to Tetra Tower. The damage boost is hefty, and they allow you to enjoy heals without bringing an extra healer like Pepper. Since you will also invest heavily in this pair (thus higher CP), they will also decrease the severity of stage penalty.","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"heading-2","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Should You Pull","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Should you pull? Yes!","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"Tia is an excellent support! A unique addition to the Meta, and the second nikke with the Re-Enter Burst I Stage skill. Although she has some problems, in the usual conditions we face in Nikke she will thrive and prove to be the best against anyone else! She seems to be an excellent addition to the roster, especially in Missilis Tribe Tower, and provides additional options to use in Union and Solo Raids. Just remember that she does need to be paired with Naga to prove herself as the ultimate support. The Tiga (Tia+Naga) pair is now, without doubt, one of the meta teams for Raids, chalking up our prediction from Naga's Review to be true!","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"If you are an F2P, we recommend getting one copy, and then wishlist her dupes if you want any. Since you will be able to wishlist her after Tia's Banner ends, we also urge you not to blindly spark her with golden tickets, unless if you already got Naga withing 10-30 pulls, and have already spent 80-90 tickets trying to get her. Any case apart from this one, we do not recommend sparking Tia with your golden mileage tickets. Anniversary is coming, so prepare in advance.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}

skillAnalysis.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Kit Analysis","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tia comes equipped with a rich kit, both offensively and defensively. We are looking at:","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill 1","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her Skill 1, which provides an immense ATK Damage buff (which is superior to ordinary ATK buffs). The uptime can be considered permanent if you pair her with certain units, especially Naga. Otherwise, without any other cover repair in team, it will only be 10s from the moment Burst Skill is activated.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"ATK Damage is a separate multiplier in the damage formula and belong to the same bracket as Parts Damage. This means it is not as diluted as ATK buffs and will noticeably multiply your damage!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"The CD part is tricky as you need to maintain two stacks at all time, which increase when cover is repaired. The problem is she only repairs cover on Burst, usually every 14~17s with CDR units, while the buff duration is only 12s! This means she should ideally be paired with units that can increment stacks (Pepper or Rupee) or units that can repair cover (Liter, Cocoa, Naga). Note that Liter's and Cocoa's cover repairs trigger every 15s, which means bad timings are bound to happen (or even worse, Tia isn't the target for that cover repair). All in all, Naga just makes activation of Tia's buffs much more simpler.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Cover MAX HP boost from her Skill 2 is NOT counted as cover repair. Be warned!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill 2","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her Skill 2, which is all about boosting her survivability. The first part is a screen-wide taunt in tandem with a brief Cover MAX HP increase. This looks too good to be true until you realize that, in some stages, the MAX HP increase may not be enough to counterbalance the damage taken. This shouldn't be a major problem against bosses, especially if the skill level and base MAX HP are high enough. You can also use her to divert missiles away from key units and i-frame them. Like usual, every time this MAX HP is triggered (provided that it expires first), it will \"regenerate\" cover HP. The regeneration is dependent on her MAX HP.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Since Tia's taunt is triggered every 5 shots, you can manual her to dodge unwanted big chunks of damage, decide when to taunt and when not to, and even reach near-perfect activation tempo if necessary (with uncharged shots). This technique is important in campaign pushing where mobs can quickly obliterate cover. Remember, the buff must first expire before being reactivated, else the cover regeneration won't happen.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"The second part is a cover repair tied to using Burst Skill, as explained when discussing Skill 1. The repair value scales up with higher base MAX HP, so make sure to raise her HP as much as needed. She also gains a brief lifesteal, which is actually trivial in short terms unless paired with units that grant profuse ATK buffs, like Liter and Naga. However, it can still make a difference in longer fights given that she is not taking too much damage.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Naga is a special case here as she provides ATK buffs based on caster's ATK, which is more beneficial in Tia's case. This is the same case as with XRupee and SAnis, who synergize with each other well. Defenders naturally have much lower offensive stats.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Burst","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her Burst, which grants a substantial shield to self and weaker shields to everyone else. These shields are Independent, which means every unit enjoys their own shield (unlike the one provided by Centi or Poli). The shields might look weak, but it can be used to absorb powerful one-shot attacks. That aside, the actual purpose of these shields is to trigger Naga's \"when applying shield\" skills, which currently has no reliable method of activation. When she and Naga are paired, you are guaranteed to activate Naga's monumental buffs all the time!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Not only that, the additional Re-Enter Burst I trait will also allow your team to benefit from an additional supportive buff of your choosing. Ideally, you would want it to be a CDR unit like Liter, Volume, or Dorothy. Mix and match your units in Raids and accumulate a huge number of buffs for your DPS every full burst. There is a minor drawback however, since the Re-Enter Burst I has a small delay which means you cannot spam the burst button, if you wanted to that.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Pairing Tia and Naga together forces you to run a 2-1-2 formation, so you can only bring 2 DPS. This limits flexibility when it comes to team composition as not many units can benefit from precision buffs like Core Damage.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Also, please remember that: ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"without cover, Tia cannot activate most of her buffs properly","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":". This means you must pay close attention to her cover HP at all times!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Gear Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tia does not need Overload to perform, but increasing her base HP will allow her to survive more easily as her shield amount, cover MAX HP bonus, and cover recovery on Burst are all dependent on it. We highly recommend OL-ing her Body Armor for the highest boost of HP. The Overload lines are not important, but prioritize MAX AMMO for more frequent S2 activation on Auto. Alternatively, you can also aim for CHARGE SPEED. If you run out of rocks, it may be better not to reroll the lines and just enjoy the increased base HP.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Body Armor provides the highest boost to HP, followed by Head and Boots. If you want to attain the highest possible increase, consider upgrading those too after maxing out the Body Armor. However, it is not really necessary.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"For smoother rotations, we highly recommend having her Skill 1 at minimum 7. This will increase the CD reduction to -13s/stack. Beyond that, level up if you want more damage boost as the independent multiplier is really valuable. As for Skill 2 and Burst, upgrades are not absolutely necessary, but they will allow Tia to survive and maintain cover longer. We recommend starting with 3 for the least amount of Blue books or 4-5 if you want to spend a bit more.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Start with 7/3/3, then 10/x/x. Upgrade to 7-10/4-5/4-5 if necessary to boost your team survivability. You can also choose to do this by upgrading her Body Armor instead and save some Skill/Burst Manuals.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Cube Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"For best performance, she is best paired with Resilience cube. Bastion can be used as an alternative and would be comparable to Resilience once her base ammo reaches 10 (from Overload).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"document"}

pros.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Provides a unique Attack Damage buff, which is rarely diluted and usually stands as an independent multiplier.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Grants Independent Shield every burst cycle, which allows the team to evade dangerous attacks over and over.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Self-sustainable thanks to multiple recovery skills (cover + lifesteal), alongside taunts to divert attacks away from key units.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Unique Re-Enter Burst Stage I trait.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Assists her major pair, Naga, to activate the dominant parts of her skills with ease.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Can provide above average burst generation in Campaign due to her being an RL; less sensitive to enemy distance.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"document"}

backstory.backstory: A Nikke acting as a new mechanic in Unlimited, which is the squad with an only drawback of continuous malfunctioning equipments. She boasts a plethora of theoretical knowledge, but lacks practical experience, which invariably leads to various mishaps. However, as an out-and-out extrovert, she is slowly but successfully fitting into the squad.

review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Foreword","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"If you want someone who is not afraid to sacrifice herself to help others, but has extremely poor sled making skills, Tove is the nikke for you! The Survivor who wouldn't survive Alone in the cold at all, has come to nikke in order to help you buff your Shotguns better than anyone else can! Her skills are a bit unique, as she has an RNG dependant skill 1 activation, but the buffs themselves are very much everything your shotgun needs! Her skill 2 will be mainly buffing the Attack Speed of your shotguns, and her Burst is a chonky Attack Buff that will make your Shotguns hit hard against anyone they're up against! However be wary, these buffs rely on her skill 1 to be stacked to give the best output! ","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Kit Analysis","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove is the currently best unit for supporting SG teams. Not only does she provide SG units a higher ATK buff compared to Liter, she also increases max ammo and overall damage dealt via ATK SPD. Her kit is designed to support SGs and only SGs (her buff is still usable outside SG, but it's very cope).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove possesses an intriguing skillset that is somewhat reliant on RNG, which means to achieve the highest damage with her, you may need to repeat your runs. This is because most of her supportive skills are locked behind 3 Stacks of Temporary Modification, whose uptime can vary sharply between runs. If Snow White drives you insane, Tove will too. Thankfully, this RNG can be attenuated slightly with the help of OL. However, before we delve into the technicalities of it, let's briefly go through her skills one by one.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill 1","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"This skill grants her the ability to randomly trigger Emergency Bullets at a 5% chance. When triggered, she reloads a certain amount of ammo and increases/refreshes the stack of Temporary Modification (abbreviated as TM in this guide), which grants increased Max Ammo to all allies for 5s. The reload helps her stack accumulation become more consistent, whereas the Max Ammo is like every other Max Ammo buff—extremely useful for units who have a low base ammo count like SG (except SAnis), SR, and RL. She also boosts the team's CRIT DMG, but the value is low.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove wields an Assault Rifle, which shoots at a firerate of 12/s (60 FPS; not FPS-friendly, by the way). Therefore, within 5s and without reloading, she blasts a maximum of 60 shots. When firing a shot, her chance of not gaining a stack is 95%. Using those variables, we can calculate that the chance of Tove not increasing/refreshing Temporary Modification when continuously shooting for 5s to be ±4.6%. If she reloads within this 5s window, it will drop to around ~7-9%, depending if she uses Resilience or Bastion.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"If Tove fails to accrue 1 stack of TM within 5s of the previous trigger, it will reset back to zero! This will result in a heavy DPS loss as it will deactivate or weaken her buffs, especially the ATK SPD in her S2 and the ATK in her Burst. She will need to trigger it again 3 times in a row. If you want to know how common this is, the estimated uptime of a base Tove is (7.7%, 7.7%, 7.7%, 77%) and an infinite ammo Tove is (5%, 5%, 5%, 85%), denoting (Stack 0, 1, 2, 3) respectively. Thank you to Titan for the simulation; here is the ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{"uri":"https://discord.com/channels/968096627002851379/1176712613556658196/1176929665391280309"},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"original post","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"hyperlink"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" in Nikke Community Discord.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill 2","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"When TM is fully stacked, Tove passively grants all allies bonus critical rate. She also grants additional ATK SPD to all allied SG. As you can see, the ATK SPD is what makes this skill worth upgrading. It functions as a separate total damage multiplier unlike most buffs in this game. According to the frame calculation formula, some levels don't actually provide a real attack speed increase. Visit Skill Investments for more detail.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"As stated in the description of Skill 1, resetting TM stacks will deactivate this buff. You will see that your SG's firerate fluctuate throughout the battle.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"blockquote"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Burst","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her Burst Skill grants an ATK buff whose effectiveness scales up with the possessed stacks of TM. The ATK buff stack mirrors TM's stack and is determined on activation; it does not dynamically update. It is guaranteed to have 1 stack on activation, even if TM has 0 stack. Therefore, you will always want to wait until Tove has 3 stacks of TM before activating her burst. Whether she loses TM stacks later on, it will not impact the given ATK buff. It still deactivates her Skill 2, regardless.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Thanks to its big numbers, this skill is what makes Tove simply irreplaceable when it comes to supporting SG units. It grants nearly 80% caster's ATK buff to all SG units in the team for 10s. If we convert this into Attacker stats, it would still amount to around 66.67%, which is superior to Liter's Burst in multiple ways. The only drawback is that, for this to be optimal, you are forced to invest in her copies and gear as her base ATK stat matters.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Usage","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove and the SGs are unlikely to be used in Campaign or Tower due to range restrictions. That said, below are some game modes they might excel in:","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"UNION RAID","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"If you have no better units for Union Raid, then Tove and the SGs can be deployed. Their damage is by no means outstanding, but it is still better than assembling a random team and praying that it will work. Avoid picking bosses that are too thin as SG requires hitting most if not all pellets to be remotely usable.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"SOLO RAID","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove and the SGs will most likely make it to the Top 5 Teams in Solo Raid, but as Team 4/5. This might change in the future if stronger SG-related units are released. Even then, this team is still terrible at dealing with thin bosses. They will be of higher value against close-range bosses, no-core bosses, or bosses with a large hitbox. Examples include Gravedigger, Modernia (when not teleporting), and so on.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"PVP","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-6"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove will probably never see the light of day in PvP meta, but if you have no one else to fill for the B1 spot, you can use Tove to help empower your SG units. However, she is handicapped in PvP. The 30 FPS limit lowers her fire rate to just 10/s, resulting in an around 50% probability of her accruing 3 stacks of TM within 5s. This means RNG may affect the outcome of a round. In the worst case, Tove does not gain any stack and becomes a sitting duck. On a totally different note, you can also pair Tove with RL and SR units, but in this case you only want to benefit from the Max Ammo buff that she provides. It's quite minuscule, but it can be the decider of the match (especially if you use Alice with a low base ammo count).","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"document"}

backstory.backstory: A Nikke acting as a new mechanic in Unlimited, which is the squad with an only drawback of continuous malfunctioning equipments. She boasts a plethora of theoretical knowledge, but lacks practical experience, which invariably leads to various mishaps. However, as an out-and-out extrovert, she is slowly but successfully fitting into the squad.

review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Can you give a brief summary about this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"The notorious Shotgun team - one that used to be the most hated team for players to use - not because of their difficulty in playing, but because of Tove’s RNG. The infamous 5% brought such a terrible experience that most didn’t even want to try using the Shotgun team - malding that run could cost as much time as other 4 runs.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"But rest assured, Treasure Tove is here to fix all your past problems. It brings the most important QoL to her: Tove’s S1 is no longer RNG but shot-based now. This is the reason why we can’t wait to deliver this review as soon as possible to you - especially after we and so many high ranking players tested her in the previous Solo Raid - Hologram Kraken.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Should I get the Favorite Item for this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"YES! She should be the top priority to upgrade in Season 4 of Favorite Items. She performs well even with just Treasure phase 1 (which all previous Treasure Nikkes don’t), and only has a bit more gain on treasure phase 2 and 3, making her power go online very soon.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Kit Analysis","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Phase 1: Changes Skill 1","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove changes her S1 from triggering with 5% chance to every 25/20/15/10 shots. This change is HUGE and we recommend you finish her treasure as soon as possible, for this change doesn’t consume any Special Treasure’s material. With this, Tove will NEVER drop stack, no matter which skill level. Let’s do some simple math:","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"25 shots will take Tove 2s to shoot","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Even if she reloads, it takes 1s.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her buff lasts 5s.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"As you can see, unless the boss jumps off screen for too long, Tove can’t drop the stack on auto. This removes completely both the OL requirement (ammo) and RNG retrying compared to original Tove. In fact, raid-wise, among all 13 treasures currently, Tove is one of the most important Nikke beside Helm to put Treasure on, with highest priority for it changes her gameplay + investment completely.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Still, we suggest leveling up this skill to lv 7 at least to lower the shooting condition to 15, so your first full burst will have max 3 stacks after 4s. Lv 9 is still the best, of course.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Phase 2: Changes Burst Skill","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"The change in phase 2 is nice, mostly supporting her burst’s buff to either last forever on CDR comp (as we saw in Hologram Kraken) or enough through full burst extension (with Bunny Soda). This makes Tove even better in buffing, and the cost is acceptable (around 18 days doing Outpost missions). Not as game changing as S1, but still a nice upgrade.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Phase 3: Changes Skill 2","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove only gains a small crit buff with this change, so it’s whatever. The cost is terrible, so you should look at other Treasure Nikkes first before finishing Tove’s phase 3 (35 more days after phase 2). There’s a change in description, but as we tested, it doesn’t affect anything more than original skill as even with it K still shoots as slow as was possible although she changes to SG during her burst.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Usage Analysis and Tier List","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Campaign (LD): S | Campaign (HD): A","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove is one of the most solid and reliable buffers especially for campaign. Her buff has insane ATK value (equals Red Hood’s B1 which has 40s cooldown), extremely rare Attack Speed, which makes her team be able to offset a lot of stat penalties… except she only supports Shotgun! The problem is not Tove, it’s that we still haven’t had any decent high tier SGs in Campaign, and that’s why, for the time being, Tove needs to stay in the lower tiers. Imagine if we had Cindy or even Rapi level of damage as SG.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Bossing - SS","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"In contrast to Campaign, Tove treasure version has a very high position in ranking. This actually doesn’t change much compared to normal Tove’s position, because instead of retrying 50 times for a maybe decent small down time without stack, you can enjoy max stack Tove from the very start. Other parts remain unchanged if not better than the original Tove.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Anyways, original Tove, great Nikke! We love her, she loves us, so we will put her to S tier. Thank you for your attention to this matter. For a detailed performance analysis for Tove on Bossing, please consider reading the guide for Tove’s normal version since it is exactly the same.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"PVP - A","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Funnily, due to how reliable Tove’s S1 is now, you can actually burst Tove with 3 stacks if your team speed is higher or equal than 2.5 RL (30 AR shots). This gives your SG team, mostly B.Soda, 71% ATK buff, along with 42% AS. This should help Soda wipe most teams, and can follow up and kill the rest with strong, fast auto attacks.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Gear Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Thanks to the change in S1, now Tove doesn’t need any specific OL. We still recommend overloading her gear to buff her Base ATK. She’s a supporter with meh modifier, so you don’t have to chase any DPS OL on her, unless you are a nut for water raids.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Essential:","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" -","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Ideal:","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" 4× ELE, 4× ATK ","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Passable:","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Hit Rate, Crit Rate, Crit DMG, Max Ammo ","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Priority:","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Low","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Skill Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"The reliable change only affects her OL requirement, you still need to upgrade her skill to squeeze the most out of her.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Skill 1: 3/6/9","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"A good start is level 3 to reduce her requirement from 25 => 20 so you don’t have to hold your first FB too long. Lv 6 will change her ammo increased from 1 => 2, and at level 9 her shot requirement goes to 10. Yeah, Tove is an odd ball.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Skill 2: 7/10","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"To be fair, Attack Speed has some check points, but over the long run, it goes quite near to the face value. Just try maximizing this skill as soon as possible.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"}],"nodeType":"list-item"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Burst Skill: 4/7/10","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Higher burst skill = higher ATK. Sadly, there’s no leeway here, just go as hard as you can.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"}],"nodeType":"list-item"}],"nodeType":"unordered-list"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Cube Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Just slap whatever you want on her for a stat stick. She deals unimportant damage anyway. Resilence, Bastion, Destructions are options for PVE and Resilence, Bastion, Vigor, Tempering are options for PVP.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Doll Investments","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Tove doesn’t need any dolls. review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"A long time ago, in 2023, it used to feel like Shift Up did not know what they were doing when they released new units. The kits of units such as Viper, Cocoa, and most of the release units were quite weak all things considered. 2 years later, in 2025, it does seem like Shift Up finally has their game figured out. They know which units need what skill to be better in the current meta, and how to make units versatile across game modes, while trying to fill in gaps of what specific type of unit we lack. This is what they do with Trina. A unit who is not overly strong, and won’t brick your account if you skip her, but is still a very usable Nikke. Let’s dive into everything we know about her!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Can you give a brief summary about this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Trina is a niche supporter B2 healer, designed to assist and buff Electric allies with assault rifles. Well, she can only buff 1 Electric ally with Assault Rifles but she does do that extremely well. Currently, Scarlet and Moran are the only two meta characters worth using with her, with more emphasis on Scarlet. Hence, in her current state, Trina is only viable if you have a clear strategy for pairing her with these key characters. For instance, she can significantly boost Scarlet’s firepower and burst damage. If you plan to rely on Scarlet’s Burst Skill to clear a challenging Campaign stage, the Trina–Scarlet combo can be a rewarding choice.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Alternatively, you can use Trina as a poor man’s Biscuit in PvP, boosting those Nikkes' survivability and enabling a stronger output. Her ATK DMG▲ will still be active, although her Burst Skill DMG▲ will not because it requires the presence of a certain number of Raptures. The ATK DMG, though, being over ~115% (with lvl 10 S2 + Burst Skill), is enough to allow Scarlet to one-shot everyone, given that the team is not protected by Noah, Bay, or Blanc. Not only that, Trina is a Clip RL.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Keep in mind, Trina is still usable without Scarlet and Moran. Most of her buffs will deactivate, but at least you will still be able to utilize her heals, a small portion of her ATK DMG▲, and Burst Skill DMG▲. However, under these circumstances, she would easily be overshadowed by alternatives such as Crown.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Should I get this unit?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"Before pulling Trina, ask yourself: Do you have Scarlet? Do you see yourself investing into her?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"In PvE content, Trina is almost ineffective without her, as her primary role is to boost Scarlet's performance and make her shine in specific scenarios, practically confirming Scarlet’s spot in lower-end teams in Electric-Weak Solo Raids. Without her, you might as well save your gems and fish her out of Ordinary using Wishlist. However, when paired with Scarlet, Trina offers tangible improvements: Her ATK DMG (and Burst Skill DMG▲) complements Scarlet's lack of ATK DMG and makes her Burst Skill satisfying again! In Campaign, this often ensures a screenwipe, allowing your team to gun down elites and bosses without worry. Yes, Trina can still be used even without Scarlet, but what makes her better than the other options? Not much.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"As a TL;DR, if you have Scarlet, we recommend pulling one copy of Trina. But, if you do not plan on using Scarlet, she is an easy skip for PvE-focused players.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"If your answer to the first question is no, we still have a saving grace second question: Do you love PvP? It is very true that Trina shines best with either Scarlet or Moran in PvP, and you definitely don't want to miss out on any Clip RL units as a PvP enthusiast. ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"A must pull unit as far as PvP is concerned!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"How about dupes?","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" Thankfully, none of Trina's essential buffs scales off her stat, which means ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"one copy of Trina is fine for everyone","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":". Her healing kind of does but small improvements in that area would be negligible. You don't even need to OL her because she doesn't contribute much damage herself, but you might need to for CP purposes in PvP.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"Is she mileage worthy?","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"Definitely not","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" in our opinion, at least for PvE-focused players. She will maybe have some uses in Campaign for Electric-weak stages, sure, but we are hard-pressed to find a spot for her in Raids outside of her own element, where she only allows Scarlet to shine. Her performance in PvP is stellar, though, especially when combined with Scarlet, where the 2s invulnerability + ATK DMG can confirm survival prior to Full Burst and instant wipes in super fast 2RL teams. Only competitive PvP players should consider using mileage on her.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Usage Analysis and Tier List","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Campaign (LD) - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"S","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":" | Campaign (HD) - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"A","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Trina can help players clear Campaign stages reliant on AoE wipes. However, she faces one glaring issue—she is heavily reliant on Scarlet. Even though she is usable without her, she is limited to being useful only for AoE screen clear units like Rei Ayanami (Tentative Name) or mediocre one trick units such as Maid Privaty, Bunny Soda, or Harran. That said, her Hit Rate▲ allows Scarlet to land core shots more, which significantly boosts her follow-up auto-attack damage, and her ATK DMG▲ + Burst Skill DMG▲ can triple her Burst Skill DMG—perfect for Electric-weak Stages!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"While that sounds remarkable, with the recent introduction of capable Nikkes, it is hard to justify slotting her in Campaign in place of a more competent B2 like Crown. Thus, we would consider her a luxury. If you plan to adopt a 1-2-2 setup, however, you can technically use Trina & Crown together, but do keep in mind that to take advantage of Trina's amazing buffs on Electric ARs, she needs to be the one bursting. Crown's Burst Skill can be used on off-rotations.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Fun fact: Thanks to Trina’s post-burst healing, Crown’s Skill 2 can passively activate and strengthen Burst Skill attacks in the second rotation onward.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Players with an incomplete roster especially in the B2 department can use Trina as a temporary B2. She is still better than most options and definitely helps with Missilis Tower if you don’t have Tia+Naga.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"Please note that Trina's Campaign (High Deficit) Rating is in accordance with a Campaign Tier List revision that is currently in the works. In the current version of the Tier List as of this review's release, she is S tier.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Bossing - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"S","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Trina is by no means a bad unit, but her impact in Bossing is inconsistent due to her skill restrictions. Trina + Scarlet is obviously the only reasonable duo we can assume here since Moran is not a PvE character. Together, they are powerful, but are they more powerful than other combinations players with a complete roster can come up with? No. Despite that, we can foresee the possibility of her being used in Electric-weak Raids, especially Electric-Weak Solo Raids, or when you need to run multiple times against an Electric-Weak boss in Union Raid, which is not optimal but sometimes you have no choice. We, however, don’t expect to see her in Neutral Element Raids at the top level.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"PVP - ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"bold"}],"value":"SS","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"When paired with Scarlet or Moran, Trina can act as a makeshift Biscuit, providing 2s invulnerability right at the start of the battle. This can prevent them from being sniped, although they would still be vulnerable after 2s have passed, so the stalling potential is weaker than Biscuit. However, it can also be used to hard-counter SG/MG teams by placing Scarlet in P1/P5 and using Trina to deny damage from the first 2 seconds, allowing Scarlet to retaliate in peace without worrying about dying to well-built SG with 4 ATK + 4 ELE.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Trina can also amplify their output through her S2 + Burst Skill buffs, giving more than 110% ATK DMG, Reload Speed▲, Ammo Up, and non-restoring Max HP. This allows Scarlet to deal much more damage with her Burst and enjoy her CRIT DMG buff early, and Moran to benefit from her DEF buffs early, making her overall tankier.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"However, do note that the Burst Skill DMG▲ for \"Affects all allies...\" does not activate in PvP, so she is not a universal buffer (well, she is, but she only gives the first part of her Burst Skill, which is not that strong alone). She can fill in as a healer, but her offensive buffs when not paired with Scarlet or Moran will be absent.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"That said, it is still justified to play Trina even without her pairs. Why is that? Well, she is a Clip RL, and we know how broken Clip RLs are for PvP! She can slot in any team as a replacement of Centi, Rumani, Jackal, and even HelmT in most team builds. A must pull unit for PvP. ‘Nuff said!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"Check PvP Team Compositions for some ideas!","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"}],"nodeType":"document"}

It's reliable because the value is not distributed (everyone gets the same amount of healing).","marks":[],"data":{}}]},{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The second one has an ambiguous description, but the effect is pretty much similar to what you might expect. review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Trony is a Fire B3 Attacker designed for ","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"value":"feet lovers","nodeType":"text"},{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":". Period. But, whether you agree with that subjective claim, it is unquestionable that Trony's enticing appearance has indeed sparked joy. ","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Summary","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-2"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"What do you think about her?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Her cost-effectiveness has much left to be desired. Trony's damage also does not scale with the number of enemies and is stagnant, unlike Scarlet with her legendary AoE wipe. Unless Elemental Type is a major issue, or ShiftUp creates a situation that favors her Cumulative Damage playstyle, her presence in the meta will be limited.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Should I pull her?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"heading-5"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Nope. Similarly, its maximum cap is determined the second this debuff is initialized based on Trony's final ATK at that moment (other DMG buffs and debuffs discounted). review.raw: {"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Velvet is an average support unit, but average in our dictionary is good, not bad. She is a niche meta—an important unit, but if you miss her as a beginner, it's fine. She's incredibly important for late game, though. A good equivalent would be SHelm or SElegg. Velvet can be used in two ways: as a support and as a DPS. As a support, she must be off-burst (you need another B2). As a DPS, she must be in-burst. There is a drawback to this, however; it's that her Burst Skill doesn't directly buff allies. No ATK, no ATK DMG. However, it dramatically increases her \"ammo consumption\", which makes units who scale off ammo consumption shine, such as Siren. Since Siren is the only ammo consumption unit now, we can say Velvet is Siren's Treasure.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Velvet is a key unit in Wind-weak Bossing with potential as an off-burst buffer in Neutral. For content where only a singular team is needed (incl. UR), Velvet is best used as an off-burst support (Siren Nayuta SBS Lib Velvet). She raises the maximum Wind-weak damage ceiling, so if you care about UR, she is important. In Raid content where you need multiple Wind teams, you can use Velvet as a support, but using her as a DPS is better. To avoid damage loss from her lack of B2 buffs, we use supportive B3 instead like HelmTr & XLud. This way, we can run MirandaTr + Nayuta + XDiesel + Maxwell hypercarry, SBS + Lib + Maids, and Siren + Velvet + HelmTr + B3 + Crown or something similar. Maybe PrivatyTr will do something?","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"In Neutral, since Velvet & Siren won't enjoy elemental buffs, Velvet can be used as an off-burst buffer similar to Maxwell. The difference is that her buff is weaker (except if the ally scales off Charge Damage) but applies to all allies. Units like RH & Alice, for example, scale better with Velvet than Maxwell and potentially Ada.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"This also explains why Velvet is relevant in Tetra Tower; the off-burst slot is still vacant. Her damage pales in comparison to Alice's and BMilk's (especially outside Water-weak), and her Damage Taken requires time to apply (that if the mob hasn't already died). To solve this issue, we alternatively use Noir, who is nifty for beginners because her ATK buff is permanent and her Ammo buff is cherished by both DPS. You no longer rely on ephemeral debuffs. Now, Noir faces a new competitor, Velvet. Velvet is an ATK-and-Charge-Damage-buffer, which makes her a good pair for Alice and Auto BMilk. Her ATK buff is stronger than Noir's despite her class, and she is technically Tetra's best Wind DPS. Noir can also beat if Alice, BMilk, or XLud (if used as a primary B3) doesn’t have enough ammo.","nodeType":"text"}],"nodeType":"paragraph"},{"data":{},"content":[{"data":{},"marks":[],"value":"Interestingly, Velvet is more beginner-friendly than many other units. Other units, such as, RRH are better for this, of course, but the lack of Max Ammo OL make them less dependable at the beginning. Velvet (esp. in Tetra Tower) also helps with breaking hitcount shields and projectiles. Dissuaded by Velvet's Burst not giving offensive buffs? Don't worry—Velvet still buffs Siren through Burst's increased ammo consumption.
